cards.front: What is the powerhouse of the cell?
cards.back: The mitochondrion — it releases energy from glucose during respiration.

cards.front: Which organelle controls all activities of the cell?
cards.back: The nucleus — it houses the chromosomes and directs cell activity.
The movement of water molecules from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential through a semi-permeable membrane.
The movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration until they are evenly spread.

cards.front: Which organelle is the site of protein synthesis?
What pigment inside chloroplasts absorbs light energy?
State the word equation for photosynthesis.
cards.back: Carbon dioxide + water, in the presence of light and chlorophyll, produce glucose and oxygen.

cards.front: What is the difference between plant and animal cell walls?
cards.back: Plant cells have a rigid cellulose cell wall outside the membrane; animal cells have no cell wall.

cards.front: What process divides one cell nucleus into two identical nuclei?
Which cell structure controls what enters and leaves the cell?
cards.back: The cell (plasma) membrane — it is partially permeable.
The oxidation of food (glucose) in cells to release energy, carbon dioxide and water.
cards.hint: Every living cell, all the time

cards.front: Name the organelle that stores water and dissolved substances in plant cells.
